title: Learned models reveal nonmonotonic bacterial patterns in boreal lakes
summary: Models fitted to observations from 70 Scandinavian lakes identified nonmonotonic associations between browning indicators and bacterial community diversity. XGBoost explained up to about 45% of community-composition variation in the analyzed data. The fitted ridges are not demonstrated causal tipping points; translating this spatial gradient into future temporal trajectories requires further validation.
ai_technology: XGBoost, random forests and feed-forward neural networks
organization: University of Oslo; Université Savoie Mont Blanc; INRAE

evidence.tested: Models analyzed field-sampled microbial communities with held-out evaluation.
evidence.unknown: Covariation, causal mechanisms and long-term temporal predictions remain unresolved.
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost, random forests and feed-forward neural networks supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher PDF abstract and selected Methods/Results/limitations; indexed publisher publication metadata. Supplements not reviewed.
